name: 20261111-spp

params: gain_rule=lsa noise_tracker=spp spp_init=lowenergy spp_direction=bidirectional spp_snr_db=10 (other SPP constants = VOICEBOX defaults)
note: Gerkmann & Hendriks, Unbiased MMSE-based noise power estimation with low complexity and low tracking delay, IEEE TASLP 20(4):1383-1393, 2012, DOI 10.1109/TASL.2011.2180896 (Crossref checked; full text not read, so constants not checked against the paper); constants from sap-voicebox voicebox/v_estnoiseg.m $Id 10865 2018-09-21 (LGPL-3, read only, re-implemented): asnr 15 dB, pspri 0.5, tax 0.0717 s, tap 0.152 s, psthr 0.99, pnsaf 0.01, tavini 0.064 s, psini 0.5; Train 18 candidates: published form (VOICEBOX init, forward) 1.698 (-0.064 vs stage 1); forward never beat stage 1; gain only from offline bidirectional + lowenergy init + xi_H1 10 dB (+0.016, Wilcoxon p 0.01, 49% files improved); Validation +0.012 (CI -0.009..0.033, p 0.56) and aircraft_cockpit n=14 -0.112 (fails -0.1 rule); wind +0.068 on both splits (Val p 0.0009); tracker underestimates stationary noise (synthetic white noise: estimate 0.78x true power; analytic E[(1-P)|Y|^2+P*sigma^2]=0.88 sigma^2 at xi_H1 15 dB)

name: 20261111-omlsa
change: gain MMSE-LSA -> OM-LSA G=G_H1^p*G_min^(1-p) (on stage 1 LSA, fixed noise)
params: gain_rule=lsa omlsa=True omlsa_spp=cohen omlsa_dd=h1 omlsa_gain_floor=0.17783 (-15 dB); Cohen q constants from BSD-3 reference
note: Cohen & Berdugo, Speech enhancement for non-stationary noise environments, Signal Processing 81(11):2403-2418, 2001, DOI 10.1016/S0165-1684(01)00128-1 (Crossref search checked; full text not read, constants not checked against the paper); q estimation and OM-LSA DD from chenwj1989/python-speech-enhancement pns/suppression_gain.py @ f38fde7 (BSD-3, (c) 2019 wjchen; re-implemented): beta 0.7, local w 1 / global w 15 Hann (MATLAB-style, no zero ends), xi thresholds -10/-5 dB, frame xi_m 0..10 dB, P_min 0.005, q_max 0.998, p=0 where q>=0.9, xi >= G_min^2, DD on G_H1^2*gamma; Train 18 candidates (spp cohen/posterior x G_min -10..-25 dB x DD h1/output): all below stage 1, best -0.033 (Wilcoxon p 2e-84, 23% files improved); stage-1 DD variant worse (best 1.704) so the loss comes from the gain blend; Validation -0.040 (CI -0.053..-0.026), 21% files improved, all six n>=10 categories down (broadband -0.050, machine -0.046, alarm_siren -0.038, wind -0.035, cockpit -0.009); IMCRA (Cohen 2003, DOI 10.1109/TSA.2003.811544, Crossref checked) not tried

name: 20261111-cepstral
change: a priori SNR: DD -> cepstro-temporal smoothing (not adopted); offline variant bidirectional DD adopted
params: gain_rule=lsa prior_snr=dd_bidir (xi = mean of forward and time-reversed stage-1 DD, then LSA with -15 dB floor)
decision: adopted (offline variant dd_bidir, pending listening check)
note: Breithaupt, Gerkmann & Martin, A novel a priori SNR estimation approach based on selective cepstro-temporal smoothing, IEEE ICASSP 2008, pp. 4897-4900, DOI 10.1109/ICASSP.2008.4518755 (DOI from authors' publication page; Crossref search rate-limited, not confirmed); full text read from the authors' PDF (inf.uni-hamburg.de): constants Table 1 (fs 16 kHz, M 512, shift M/2; alpha_const 0.5/0.7/0.97 for q 0-2/3-19/20-256, alpha_pitch 0.2, beta 0.96, dq 2, Lambda_thr 0.2, f0 70-300 Hz, tau_H 8, xi_min -25 dB, xi_ml_min -27 dB, kappa 0.5*Euler); Hamming window normalisation in eq. 8 not stated (normalised chosen: 27% vs 92% noisy frames voiced); paper used Wiener gain, G_min -17 dB, noise by minimum statistics; we keep stage-1 LSA -15 dB and the fixed noise estimate; Train: cepstral basic 1.7259 (-0.037), best cepstral (per-frame constants, kappa 1x) 1.7546 (-0.008, p 0.92); ml_2d 1.61-1.63; dd_bidir 1.7709 (+0.008, p 1.6e-18, 63% files improved); Validation dd_bidir +0.009 (CI 0.000..0.018), 67% improved, SNR +0.26 dB; n>=10 categories cockpit +0.034 alarm +0.022 broadband +0.032 wind +0.022 machine -0.001; Train vehicle_interior (n=19) -0.088; dd_bidir has no literature support (skill roadmap offline variant); also fixed tools/evaluate.py --set for bool values

name: 20261111-tonal
change: noise-type module for the weakest type (alarm_siren): long narrowband peak tracks added to the noise PSD (on stage 4: LSA + dd_bidir)
params: gain_rule=lsa prior_snr=dd_bidir tonal_module=True tonal_level=track_median tonal_peak_db=10 tonal_min_seconds=1.0
note: weakest type chosen from data: alarm_siren lowest Validation gain over noisy among n>=10 (+0.273, n=23) and lowest Train PESQ among large types (n=187); bell (Train n=15, -0.018) is also tonal; peak tracking after McAulay & Quatieri, Speech analysis/synthesis based on a sinusoidal representation, IEEE TASSP 34(4):744-754, 1986, DOI 10.1109/TASSP.1986.1164910 (Crossref checked; full text not read, so the matching rule constants are our own: peak >= 10 dB over 15-bin median, matching interval 2 bins/8 ms, gap 2 frames, main lobe +-2 bins, 100-7800 Hz); skill gives no reference for this module; detector marks 5.6% of bins on siren clips, 1.9% bell, ~0.6% on clean speech (false hits on long low-frequency harmonics); Train 11 candidates all below stage 4 (observed level: 1.53-1.76, SNR down to 5.7 dB; track_median level: 1.711-1.763); best track_median 1 s: -0.008 (p 2.5e-4), alarm_siren -0.013 n.s., bell +0.015 n.s.; Validation -0.013 (CI -0.027..0.000, p 0.017), SNR -0.89 dB, alarm_siren +0.007 n.s.; stationary alarm tones are already in the fixed noise estimate, so the module adds little on sirens and removes speech harmonics elsewhere

name: 20261111-phase
change: phase reconstruction in voiced speech (on stage 4: LSA + dd_bidir)
params: gain_rule=lsa prior_snr=dd_bidir phase_reconstruction=True phase_mode=frequency phase_smooth=True phase_fade_frames=3 phase_max_hz=600
note: Krawczyk & Gerkmann, STFT phase reconstruction in voiced speech for an improved single-channel speech enhancement, IEEE/ACM TASLP 22(12):1931-1940, 2014, DOI 10.1109/TASLP.2014.2354236 (Crossref checked; full text read from the authors' PDF, inf.uni-hamburg.de): eqs. 8, 11, 13, Sec. IV-A3 window phase by zero padding, Sec. IV-B combined method, H=floor(4000/f0); paper setup 8 kHz, 32 ms / 4 ms shift, sqrt-Hann, noisy amplitude, PEFAC f0; ours 16 kHz, 32 ms / 8 ms Hann (unchanged), LSA amplitude, YIN f0 (de Cheveigne & Kawahara, JASA 111(4), 2002; DOI not separately checked) because PEFAC's voicing decision uses a trained model; YIN threshold 0.1 and -30 dB gate our choices; zero-padded boundary frames excluded (they broke the along-time recursion in a synthetic test); synthetic harmonic test: across-frequency reconstruction exact (0.000 rad), combi 0.0007 rad; Train 9 candidates: paper combi 1.7545 (-0.016, SNR 6.7 dB: along-time propagation diverges on real f0 tracks), frequency-only 4 kHz 1.7683; offline f0 smoothing + 3-frame crossfade + lower harmonic limit monotone better (4k 1.7715, 2k 1.7723, 1k 1.7739, 600 Hz 1.7743, +0.0034, Wilcoxon p 9e-14); Validation +0.0045 (CI 0.0008..0.0084, p 0.0036, 63% improved), n>=10 categories wind +0.010 machine +0.008 cockpit +0.004 alarm +0.004 broadband -0.006; literature gain (+0.2) not reproduced with LSA amplitudes

note: Candes, Li, Ma & Wright, Robust principal component analysis?, J.
